openai.feedback:
- Category: spec
- Severity: medium
- File: client/src/pages/TriagePage.tsx:61 — `tile` state
- Finding: Clicking “Critical + High” creates an active filter stored only in component state. Reloading or navigating away resets it, despite the requirement that Triage filters survive reload and navigation.
- Suggestion: Represent this tile selection in the persisted view, or implement it through the persisted severity filter.

- Category: bug
- Severity: medium
- File: client/src/lib/triageBoardModel.ts:68 — `matchesSearch(e, q)`
- Finding: Search hides returned parks before the tile bypass is evaluated. With more than 12 open items, entering a query that does not match a returned item makes it disappear, violating the retained “a returned park always shows” behavior.
- Suggestion: Apply the returned-park bypass around the complete search-and-tile predicate. Add a pipeline test combining search with a nonmatching returned park.

- Category: regression
- Severity: medium
- File: client/src/pages/TriagePage.tsx:132 — `showEmpty` calculation
- Finding: The empty-state condition uses visible parked items rather than the unfiltered parked population. If there are only dateless parks and an attribute filter excludes them, the page says “No triage items pending. ✓” even though pending items exist. The previous implementation explicitly distinguished this from a genuinely empty queue.
- Suggestion: Base the genuine-empty state on both unfiltered populations. Show a filtered-out state with a working clear-filters action when filters hide the remaining parked items.

- Category: test
- Severity: medium
- File: client/src/lib/triageHelpText.ts:250 — `KNOWN_CHECK_CODES`
- Finding: The known-code catalog is derived from the help entries themselves, so the coverage test cannot detect a known producer code that lacks help. Scanning the historical triage log only catches codes already emitted there; an omitted known check that has never failed still passes.
- Suggestion: Obtain the known-code set independently from the audit producers or a canonical catalog, then assert that every code has an explicit help entry.

Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The implementation covers most of the redesign, but filter persistence, returned-item visibility, empty-state correctness, and the required help-coverage guard need specific corrections.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

glm.feedback:
### Findings

- Category: test
  Severity: medium
  File: client/src/lib/triageHelpText.test.ts:16 (`const LOG = resolve(__dirname, "../../../.shipwright/triage.jsonl")`)
  Finding: The coverage test does `readFileSync(LOG)` on the repository's own working-tree triage log. In a clean checkout / CI clone where that file is absent (it is a local artifact, not committed test data), the test throws ENOENT and fails the suite — not because a code lacks help text, but because the fixture doesn't exist.
  Suggestion: Guard the read (`existsSync`) and skip (or assert against a committed fixture list) when the log is absent, so the test enforces coverage where the data exists without hard-failing otherwise.

- Category: test
  Severity: medium
  File: client/e2e/flows/triage-redesign.spec.ts:157-162 ("Fix now … for the entry's own project")
  Finding: The test's name promises the fix-now dialog opens bound to the entry's own project, but it only asserts `getByRole("dialog")` is visible. A regression that binds fix-now to the page-level/scope project (the exact cross-project-id hazard this redesign calls out) would still pass.
  Suggestion: Assert the project preselect inside the dialog (e.g. the NewIssueModal's selected project equals the seeded project, including a second seeded project so the wrong binding is distinguishable).

- Category: bug
  Severity: medium
  File: client/src/components/triage/TriageActiveFilters.tsx:82-88 (`onClick={() => { view.clearFilters(); onClearTile?.(); }}`)
  Finding: The chips bar's "Clear filters" clears attribute filters and the tile but not the search text. With an active search hiding items, "Showing 0 of N" (or a partially narrowed list) survives "Clear filters" with no chip representing the cause — the very "invisible filter" problem the component's own docstring says it exists to prevent.
  Suggestion: Either clear the search too (lift it or pass an `onClearSearch`), or render a removable "Search: …" chip alongside the others.

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: medium
  File: client/src/components/triage/TriageViewMenus.tsx:103-119 (native `<select>` inside `Popover.Content`)
  Finding: A native `<select>` inside a Radix `Popover.Content` is a known trap: opening the option list registers as an outside interaction and can close the popover (and on some platforms focus loss) before `onChange` fires, making the Sort menu's key selects unreliable, particularly on mobile — and there is no E2E/unit coverage exercising the Sort popover selects (only grouping is E2E'd).
  Suggestion: Verify on the real stack; if it closes, render the sort keys as menu items or add `onInteractOutside`/`modal={false}` handling, and add an E2E that changes the primary sort key through the popover.

- Category: bug
  Severity: low
  File: client/src/pages/TriagePage.tsx (`hiddenTotal` computation near `showFilteredOut`)
  Finding: The all-filtered-out message says "N hidden by the active filters", but `hiddenTotal = openAll − visibleOpen (+ hiddenParked)`, which also counts items narrowed away by the *search* and the *tile* — copy promises filters only.
  Suggestion: Either exclude search/tile from the count, or word it neutrally ("hidden by the current view").

- Category: bug
  Severity: low
  File: client/src/components/triage/TriageQuickEdit.tsx:41-44 (`const [initial] = useState(item); const [title, setTitle] = useState(item.title)`)
  Finding: `initial` is captured once per popover body mount. If the 30 s poll replaces the item (or another surface amended it) while the popover is open, the change-diff is computed against the stale snapshot — the user "saves" a title/severity relative to an outdated baseline and can silently clobber a concurrent amend.
  Suggestion: Diff against the *current* `item` prop (or key the `Body` on the item's amendedAt/id so it remounts when the item changes).

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: low
  File: client/e2e/flows/triage-redesign.spec.ts:76-78 (`afterEach` / `project` cleanup)
  Finding: If `beforeEach` fails before `seedProject` resolves, `project` is undefined and `cleanupProject(request, project)` throws in cleanup, masking the original failure with an opaque TypeError.
  Suggestion: Guard `afterEach` with `if (project) …` (or initialize `project` to a sentinel) so the real failure surfaces.

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: low
  File: client/src/components/triage/TriageItemCard.tsx (card `<article onClick …>`)
  Finding: The card body lost `data-nav-item` and any keyboard-accessible activation it had as a `<button>`; the title button remains the keyboard path, but focus/keyboard-nav regressions in the card body (e.g. voice-control "click the card") are unfenced.
  Suggestion: Confirm the keyboard-nav test suite still covers the card, or add `role`/`tabindex` handling for the body click.

### Notes on what's solid

The core pipeline (`triageBoardModel` → filter/search/tile/sort/group), include-set filter semantics, both park bypasses (including inside collapsed groups and the tile), cross-project id keying, the validated localStorage round-trip with per-field fallbacks, and the snooze calendar math are all well implemented and genuinely tested — the tests assert behavior (visible ids, counts, persistence across remount), not mocks. The AC list is otherwise fully covered, including the >12 search threshold and the help-text coverage gate.

Overall: the redesign is implemented and well-tested; the issues above are mostly test-environment fragility and secondary affordances rather than broken core behavior — ship-with-fixes.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
